capabilities.target: ERP vendor master record, including bank details
Vendor bank details in ERP vendor master record
Vendor payment (wire/ACH to vendor bank account)

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: 'If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record' gives no verification step for invoice authenticity before changing payment routing; the goal of updating bank details is driven directly by untrusted document content.

The entire safety control for payments and bank changes is a model-written 'one line summary so the clerk can approve quickly.' Nothing structural requires the summary to disclose that a bank account changed, so the gate's effectiveness depends entirely on the model's compliance and completeness.

elements.name: Scheduled payment sent to vendor bank account
ERP vendor master record (including bank details)

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The clerk approves based solely on a model-written one-line summary that omits bank account details and change history; a more capable model can write more persuasive or selectively incomplete summaries (ASI09). Approval volume of ~150 cards/day also produces consent fatigue (SAFE-T1403) that erodes scrutiny independent of model capability.

controls.name: Out-of-band bank detail change confirmation bound to vendor's known contact
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model via a separate verified channel independent of invoice content; does not weaken as the model becomes more capable.

controls.name: Raw-action approval review for bank changes (full details, change history, invoice image)
controls.decay_rationale: Shows the approver the actual destination and change history rather than a model summary, removing dependence on the model's honesty or persuasiveness.

controls.name: Hard spend cap / dual control threshold on scheduled payments
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced in the ERP/payment rail outside the model; limits maximum loss regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Least-privilege ERP credential scoped by vendor category / transaction limits
controls.decay_rationale: A scoped credential removes capability entirely regardless of model compliance; it does not decay with model upgrades.

controls.name: Tamper-evident, attributable audit log of bank changes and payment approvals
controls.decay_rationale: A store-level, tamper-evident log does not decay with model capability; it is detective rather than preventive.

controls.name: Rate limit on vendor bank detail changes per vendor per time window
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model in the ERP integration layer; narrows the window for repeated or duplicate fraudulent changes regardless of model behavior.

findings.title: Confused deputy (TC4): invoice-driven vendor bank redirection and payment using an over-privileged ERP credential, gated only by a model-summary approval

attack_path.note: Attacker submits a fraudulent invoice through the supplier portal showing new bank details for an existing vendor (Northwind Supplies).
Agent reads the vendor master record, including bank details, using a broad ERP credential that can read any vendor.
Agent updates the vendor's bank details based solely on invoice content, gated by a clerk approval card showing only a one-line summary that omits the bank account change.
Agent schedules payment to the newly updated (attacker-controlled) bank account on the due date, gated by the same kind of one-line summary approval.

forecast.watch_signal: Model or platform version changes (subject.model.swappable is true, no separate review gate), approval volume rising further above ~150/day, or the approval gate being removed or narrowed.

evidence.observation: Instruction says 'If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record,' driving bank detail updates directly from untrusted invoice content with no independent verification step specified.
Approval request uses 'a one line summary so the clerk can approve quickly,' establishing a model-summary gate rather than raw-action review.
The sample card shows only vendor name, amount, and PO match; it does not disclose that a bank account was changed.
States bank account numbers and change history are not shown to the clerk, approval volume is ~150 cards/day, and the ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment.

recommendations.action: Require out-of-band verification (e.g., a callback to a vendor contact on file, independent of the invoice) before any bank detail change takes effect.
Convert the approval gate for bank changes and payments to raw-action review, showing the actual bank account, change history, and invoice image, not a one-line model summary.
Scope the ERP credential to least privilege per vendor category/amount, and add a hard spend cap or dual control for payments above a risk threshold.

findings.title: No tamper-evident record attributing bank detail changes and payment approvals to specific actors

forecast.watch_signal: No change expected from these triggers alone; watch for any future logging capability being added and then later disabled without review.

evidence.observation: States that bank account numbers and change history are not shown to the clerk, and gives no indication that bank changes or approvals are recorded in a tamper-evident, individually attributable log.

recommendations.action: Implement tamper-evident, individually attributable logging of all agent-initiated vendor record changes and clerk approval decisions.

findings.title: No rate, volume, or spend-cap limit on invoice-triggered bank changes or payments

forecast.watch_signal: Watch invoice volume per vendor per day and the number of bank-detail changes or payment schedules triggered without an enforced cap.

evidence.observation: Describes a broad ERP credential that can update any vendor and schedule any payment, with no mention of a rate, volume, or spend-cap limit on how many such actions can be taken.

recommendations.action: Add a rate limit on bank detail changes and a per-vendor/per-day spend cap on payments triggered by invoice processing, enforced outside the model.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how the agent authenticates to the ERP system or whether its process identity could be spoofed by another integration; no auth method is documented.
No capability in this design returns vendor bank details or other confidential data to the invoice submitter or any external party; the only external movement is the payment itself.
Artifacts do not describe whether the supplier portal authenticates uploaders or retains non-repudiable records of who submitted each invoice.
Artifacts do not describe authentication controls on the approval card interface, so impersonation of the approving clerk cannot be assessed.
The invoice flow carries content into the agent only; no channel in this design routes that content or derived vendor data back out to the submitter or a third party.
Sending payment instructions to the vendor's bank is the capability's intended function and discloses no more confidential data than a legitimate payment requires.
Vendor master reads are used only internally for invoice-to-PO matching; no capability in this design returns vendor master contents to an external party.

rating.rationale: An untrusted invoice (U source) can reach a severe sink (irreversible payment via a broad, shared ERP credential) in a few steps, giving inherent risk of critical. The only declared control is a clerk approval gate, which earns step-2 credit (-1 tier for high-volume, model-summary review), bringing residual to high. Two property gaps (no attributable audit trail; no rate or spend-cap limit) sit at high on their own. Because the approval gate is partially dependent on model capability and review mode, a model upgrade, autonomy increase, or removal of the gate would eliminate its credit entirely, returning the path finding to its inherent critical tier; forecast is set to critical accordingly.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (system prompt, approval card example, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.
No MCP/tool manifest or IaC was provided; exact ERP credential scoping and tool schemas are inferred from the runtime notes, which reduces confidence on some details.
No logging or audit configuration was provided, so repudiation and detection capabilities are assessed as absent rather than verified.
